t: Romanos had split his army before the battle, and the Byzantine reserve under Andronikos Doukas withdrew to the camp instead of covering the retreat, which left the rest of the line exposed.

Modern scholars estimate that Byzantine losses were relatively low and that many units fought elsewhere within a few months. The lasting damage came from the civil war that followed, which the Seljuks used to their advantage.
Later Byzantine writers called Manzikert a disaster and greatly exaggerated the numbers of troops and casualties; Delbrück thought the battle's importance exaggerated.
dyk: It was the only time a Byzantine emperor became the prisoner of a Muslim commander, and the first time since Valerian that a Roman emperor was captured alive by an enemy force.
ev: Constantine IX disbands the "Iberian Army", which Skylitzes puts at 50,000 men
Alp Arslan attacks the theme of Iberia and takes Ani after a siege of 25 days
Romanos IV Diogenes takes power and begins two major campaigns against the Seljuks and their Mirdasid allies
Romanos's army reaches Theodosiopolis and the march continues towards Lake Van
Romanos takes Manzikert and his army is defeated by the Seljuks nearby
Romanos is released after a week, loses three battles to the Doukas family, and is deposed and blinded
The Seljuks establish their capital at Nikaea
The First Crusade begins as a western response to the Byzantine emperor's call for help

f.place: Near Manzikert, in the theme of Iberia, modern Malazgirt in Muş Province, eastern Turkey
f.sides: The Byzantine Empire under the emperor Romanos IV Diogenes, with a host of around 40,000 men before it was divided; the Seljuk Empire under the sultan Alp Arslan, with allies and 30,000 cavalry from Aleppo and Mosul, joined by a force of Kurdish fighters estimated at 10,000 sent by the Marwanid emir
f.outcome: The Byzantine army was routed and Romanos IV was wounded and taken prisoner. After a week he was released on agreed terms, but he was soon deposed and blinded in a civil war.
